The week the tape faded the crowd.

It was an opportunity-rich week that punished anyone who confused a spike for a trend. Only 46% of the 94 gappers closed above their 9:30 open, and just 37% finished above their session VWAP. The median stock still offered +8.9% of max upside off the open — there were trades to be made — but the median giveback from the day's high all the way through after-hours was -11.3%. Translation: the move was real, but it was front-loaded, and longs who didn't take profits early gave back almost everything by the close.

The chart-of-the-week is a histogram, not a price line. 61% of names put in their high of day inside the first sixty minutes; 52% did it inside the first thirty. After 10:30 ET the odds of a fresh high collapsed for most of the universe — only the genuine continuation runners (RDAC, HTCO, AIOS) kept making higher highs into the afternoon. If you weren't long by 10:30 on those names, you weren't long.

● TIME OF DAY HIGH — 30-MIN BUCKETS

If it works, it works fast.

This was two different weeks.

Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday all closed with negative median intraday moves — -5.6%, -3.0%, and a brutal -7.1% respectively. Then on Thu the tape flipped: 56% of names closed green, median move +1.2%. Friday held the bid too. A trader paying attention to daily tape quality could have sized down through the first half of the week, added on Thursday's strength, and walked out flat or better. A trader sized up early got hit.

● MEDIAN INTRADAY MOVE BY DAY

The tape flipped on Thu.

The premarket rip is a setup, not an entry.

The single most repeated pattern of the week: the gap was already half-faded by the time regular trading started. 94% of these gappers had a premarket high that sat above the 9:30 open — meaning the early-bird premarket move had already cooled by the bell. The median fade from premarket peak to the 9:30 open was -5.7%. If you saw a name ripping at 8:45 a.m. and chased it into the open, you were buying the high. The premarket told you which names had attention; price action after 9:30 told you whether to actually buy.

"If you saw a name ripping at 8:45 a.m. and chased it into the open, you were buying the high."

Pattern mattered more than gap size.

The cleanest signal of the week was structural, not cosmetic. The 8 Gap-and-go names — opened, broke the first 15-minute high, and never gave it back — had a median intraday of +49.5% and a median Long Score of 94. The 21 Reclaim setups — names that dipped below the 9:30 open and then took it back — put up +13.2%. The 11 Long traps — names that closed −15% or worse — printed their high at the bell and never recovered, with a median move of -26.0%. And the 42 names tagged Chop went nowhere clean, finishing -5.8% on average. Pick the pattern, not the percentage gap.

What kind of news worked.

The catalysts that paid this week shared a shape: concrete deal terms or a clean sector-sympathy thesis. M&A / Deal headlines (YAAS, RDAC) had a median intraday of +128.2%. Sector / Theme plays (HTCO, FCEL) put up +106.0% — lithium expansion and AI-data-center fuel cells, two themes the market keeps rewarding. On the trap side, Restructuring / Earnings (WTO) and Capital structure stories were where longs got hurt — turnaround promises with integration risk, registered-direct offerings, and reverse-split mechanics all produced violent fades after their first liquidity wave.

The takeaway isn't subtle. Treat the catalyst as a watchlist builder, not an entry signal. Wait for the breakout. Sell into extension. Respect the premarket high as supply. Skip capital-structure stories or size them like options. And the names that do earn a position — pick the ones with a real pattern under them, not just the biggest premarket print.

VERDICT
The week's tape was fade-friendly. Only 46% of the 94 gappers closed green and just 37% finished above their session VWAP, while 61% printed their high inside the first hour — a textbook gap-and-fade week. Median giveback from the day's high all the way through after-hours was -11.3% (-10.9% during regular hours, another -0.98% after the bell), and 67% of names continued lower in AH — so longs that didn't take profits early ate the second leg, and overnight holders ate a third. The tape flipped on Thu (2026-04-30, median +1.2%); the worst long day was Wed (2026-04-29, median -7.1%).

What a successful long-biased day trader would have done this week

The winning behavior was not prediction. It was preparation, confirmation, fast profit-taking, and refusing to let a catalyst override the tape.

Treat the catalyst as a watchlist builder, not an entry signal.

The names with real continuation (RDAC, HTCO, AIOS, YAAS, SEGG) all had a clear public catalyst — SPAC mergers, voting-power proposals, deal news. The catalyst told you to watch. Price action after the bell told you whether to buy.

Buy strength after reclaim or continuation, not every gap.

57.4% of names made a new high after the first 15 minutes, yet the median close was -0.9%. The better longs were the ones that kept accepting higher prices after the first push — Reclaim and Gap-and-go patterns combined had a median Long Score in the 80s.

Sell into extension. Don't turn day trades into opinions.

Median max upside was +8.9% but median giveback (incl AH) was -11.3%. Scaling out into strength beat waiting for perfection.

Respect the premarket high as supply.

94% of gappers had a PM high above the regular-session open — meaning the early-bird PM rip had already faded by 9:30. Median fade from PM high to 9:30 open: -5.7%. Clean reclaim was constructive; rejection there was the obvious short setup.

Size down on capital-structure stories.

Reverse splits (TLIH), offerings (WTO), SPAC mechanics (RDAC), voting-control proposals (AIOS), and thin-float warrants showed up repeatedly. They created violent opportunity and violent rug-pulls. Smaller size, faster profit-taking, demand more confirmation.

Lean harder Thu/Fri, lighter Mon-Wed.

Close quality flipped late: 56% green Thursday, 60% green Friday, vs 31-41% Mon-Wed. A trader paying attention to daily tape quality could have pressed when conditions improved and stayed defensive when closes were weak.

Performance by pattern six-bucket structural read

Every event is tagged with a structural pattern based on its intraday behavior: Gap-and-go = closed +25% with new high after the first 30 min. Reclaim = dipped below open then closed +5%. Controlled trend = closed green with shallow drawdown. Pop then fade = max upside ≥20% then closed red. Long trap = closed ≤ −15%. Chop = none of the above. The takeaway: this is a sharper edge than gap-size.

Key takeaways for longs

  • The fade didn't stop at 4 PM. 67% of names continued lower in after-hours (median -0.98% on top of the regular-session loss). Including AH, the median giveback from the day's high is -11.3%, not the -10.9% you'd see if you only looked at 9:30–4. Holding overnight made it worse.
  • The premarket rip is a setup, not an entry. 94% of gappers had a premarket high above the regular-session open. Median fade from PM high to 9:30 open was -5.7% — so by the time the bell rings, you've already missed half the move. Use PM to spot the name, not to chase it.
  • Price tier mattered more than gap size. $10+ names closed green 70% of the time with a +5.4% median intraday move. Sub-$10 names (71 of 94) only closed green 38% of the time. If you're long-only, the higher-priced tier was the only place to be.
  • The biggest gappers offered the biggest swings. The 50–100% gap bucket (8 names) had a median +32.4% max upside off the open — meaning a disciplined long with a quick exit could have caught real moves. But the median giveback was -28.8%, so the trade was front-loaded.
  • If it's going to work, it works fast. 52% of names printed HOD in the first 30 minutes. After 10:30 ET, the odds of a fresh high collapsed for most names — only the true continuation runners (RDAC, HTCO, AIOS) made HODs after 11:00.
  • This was two different weeks. Mon–Wed median intraday was negative every day (worst: -6.1% Wed). Thu and Fri flipped positive (+1.2% and +1.1%). If you sized down through the first half and added on Thu strength, the week was survivable. If you sized up early, you got hit.

Glossary

Sessions
Pre-market = 04:00–09:30 ET · Regular (RS) = 09:30–16:00 ET · After-hours (AH) = 16:00–20:00 ET.
Gap %
Pre-market reference price vs. prior session close. Only gap-ups ≥10% are scanned.
Intraday %
9:30 open → 4 PM close. The clean read on whether the gap was bought or sold during regular hours.
Max Upside
day high vs. 9:30 open. The most a long could have made off the regular-session open.
Giveback (incl AH)
day high → AH close. The full pain a long who held into AH actually saw.
AH Move
4 PM close → AH close. How much further the stock moved after the bell.
PM High
Highest pre-market print. Often above the 9:30 open — meaning the early-bird premarket move had already faded by 9:30.
HOD<1h
% of names that put in their RS high of day inside the first 60 minutes.
% Bars Abv VWAP
% of RS 5-min bars that closed above session VWAP. Cleanest trend read.
